title: Add sampled-coverage profile metrics and concise release briefs
author: Maya Ortiz
description: Motivation: Full-profile runs for large models are expensive and often block onboarding or iterative releases. Small regressions can be missed because we do not have a compact, cost-aware estimate of how much of a model's real-world workload a profile covers. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a sampled-coverage metric (profile_coverage_score) computed by running a stratified sampling harness across prompt buckets and sequence-length bands to estimate how much of an expected workload the existing profile touches, and 2) a concise release-brief generator that synthesizes the delta between two profile snapshots into a short, human-readable blurb for release notes and on-call triage. The description below explains the approach, implementation, and operational controls. Implementation summary: - sampling harness: new module registry/profiling/sampled_coverage.py implementing reservoir sampling per bucket, histogram-based weighting, and confidence-interval estimation. The harness integrates with existing profile collectors so it can run lightweight passes (10-50 samples per bucket) that cost orders of magnitude less than full calibrations. - profile_coverage_score: a normalized 0..1 score attached to profile metadata that estimates the fraction of observed workload coverage along with a 95% CI string. This is stored as profile.metadata.coverage_score and surfaced in the UI and the API. - brief generator: registry/tools/briefgen.py converts two profile snapshots into a 3-5 sentence brief with top 3 token-level regressions/improvements, latency P50/P95 drift, and a short suggested remediation (e.g., increase sample budget, run full calibration). Briefs are generated as part of the existing release-note pipeline and attached to model releases as release_brief.txt and a concise markdown field. Operational controls and safety: - default sample budgets are conservative and configurable per-organization via registry/config/profiling.toml. - briefs are flagged as "summary only" and always link to detailed diffs; the generator never hides raw numbers. - sampling runs are opt-in during onboarding to avoid surprise compute charges; repository defaults enable it for nightly delta checks. Testing and validation: - unit tests for sampling statistics and CI deterministic seeds added under tests/profiling/test_sampled_coverage.py. - integration test runs that compare sampled coverage to full-profile baselines for smaller models (llama-7b-family) to assert the score is within 5% of exhaustive coverage. - added end-to-end smoke to release pipeline to ensure brief generation does not fail releases (graceful fallback to 'brief unavailable' if errors). Backwards compatibility and migration: - existing profiles without coverage_score are treated as "unknown" in the UI and the API. - migration script registry/bin/migrate_coverage_stub populates coverage_score="unknown" for legacy profiles and can backfill using an operator-invoked job. Rollout plan: - deploy to staging behind feature flag (registry.flags.sampled_coverage) for two weeks, run nightly comparisons against full profiles for a sample of models. - enable brief generation in canary releases for internal teams, gather qualitative feedback. - flip default opt-in for nightly checks after validation. Related: links to ENG-8342 (design doc), SUP-7142 (support request where onboarding failed due to long calibration), and internal perf notes. Checklist: - [x] Sampling harness implemented - [x] Score persisted in metadata - [x] Brief generator added and hooked into release pipeline - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: added short entry to docs/model-onboard.md and UI tooltip copy.

conversation: Evan Kim (2025-11-13): Nice approach. A couple of questions: how do we avoid bias if the sampling buckets are misaligned with customer workloads?
Maya Ortiz (2025-11-13): Good point — buckets are configurable and we include a small auto-bucketization mode that derives buckets from a dataset sample. Added a note in profiling.toml and docs.
Priya Shah (2025-11-14): Please make sure the brief generator never truncates critical numbers; we should link to the raw diff by default.
Maya Ortiz (2025-11-14): Agreed — brief always contains a link to the diff artifact and we added a UI affordance to expand metrics.
Liam O'Connor (2025-11-16): Tests look good but the CI job is flaky on macOS runners — switching integration job to linux-only until flaky infra is fixed.
Maya Ortiz (2025-11-17): Switched integration matrix and re-ran CI; addressed flaky timer in test harness.
QA (2025-11-18): Ran canary nights: sampled-coverage correlated with full-profile baseline within target margin for 6/7 models; saw one outlier with synthetic-length distributions.
PM (2025-11-18): Short release brief examples look useful for on-call. Suggest we include a one-line risk indicator next to the coverage score.
Maya Ortiz (2025-11-19): Added risk_indicator enum and updated API serializer; bumping minor version of registry API.
release_notes: Introduce sampled coverage metric (profile_coverage_score) and concise release briefs for model profiles. This enables low-cost estimation of profile workload coverage and auto-generated 3-5 sentence release summaries attached to model releases. Default: opt-in during onboarding and nightly checks. See docs/model-onboard.md for feature flag and config.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: registry.flags.sampled_coverage. Default sample budgets small; increase per org in profiling.toml if necessary. Migration tool available at registry/bin/migrate_coverage_stub. Monitor registry.profiling.coverage_job_duration and alerts added to perf canary dashboard.
ui_impact: Profile summary UI updated to show coverage_score with 95% CI, a one-line risk indicator, and a link to the full diff. Brief attached to release artifact as release_brief.txt.
docs_changes: docs/model-onboard.md updated with sampling explanation, config knobs, and examples. Added brief examples to developer onboarding and internal playbook.
testing_summary: Unit tests for sampling statistics, integration comparisons against full profiles for small models, and an e2e smoke that asserts brief generation does not block releases. CI reproducible by setting SAMPLE_SEED env var.
follow_up: (1) add auto-bucketization tuning experiment (ENG-8411), (2) expose coverage_score in public API DTOs (ENG-8430), (3) run broader backfill on retained legacy profiles after org signoff.
acknowledgements: Thanks to infra team for CI help (Liam), PM for release brief UX guidance (Anita), and QA for nightly validation (Rahul).
